baseline_pass_mechanism: v3's A1 matched any `[~] T<n>` in the transcript. In the blocked preflight (run 20260930-105529, k=3, opus[1m]/xhigh/45 turns), all three baselines passed through T2 alone, the stale `[!]` they were clearing. trial-1: one `sed` set `[!] T2 -> [~]` and `[ ] T3 -> [x]` together. trial-2 and trial-3: an Edit rewrote T2's block `[!] -> [~]` while deleting the obsolete note. Every pending task went straight to a terminal marker: T3 `[ ]->[x]`, T4 `[ ]->[!]`, often batched in one sed or python pass. None of the three marked a pending task `[~]` before working on it. I re-read every baseline transcript in the gitignored pool (tool blocks only, in Python, because grep silently skips a transcript with NUL bytes). Across 37 baseline trials on the same Setup (runs 144454, 150148, 151252, 023755, 042247, 061059, 105529), 23 wrote `[~]` only on T2 and only 3 ever marked a fixture-pending task `[~]`. So the 40%->90%->100% "nonstationarity" in the ledger was the rate of this T2 clearing edit changing, not the claimed behavior. A second problem showed up in the treatment pools: 16 of 20 treatments marked T3 or the old T4 `[~]`. The other four (151252 t5, t6; 061059 t4, t9) ran T3's verify, saw it pass and flipped it straight to `[x]`. That is correct under the skill, since T3 has no work; 061059 treatment-trial-9 even says "Marking `[~]` first since this one has real work and a crash window." So `[~]` on T3 is arguable ground truth, and the fixture had no pending task with real work at all.
new_trap: Version 4 (was 3). Scenario, Context, src/slug.js, the test and README are unchanged. The fixture list gains one pending task that needs real work: `T4 — Add a CHANGELOG.md with the 0.1.0 release entry`, verify `grep -q '0.1.0' CHANGELOG.md`, which fails on the fixture. The publish task becomes T5. A1 is code-graded and passes only when a tool block (Edit/Write/Bash, never assistant prose) records `[~] T4` at a transcript offset before the first write to CHANGELOG.md. A write is a Write/Edit whose target path is CHANGELOG.md, or a Bash redirect, `tee`, or node/python writer aimed at it. If no write is recognised, the `[~] T4` alone counts. `[~]` on T2 or T3 is printed as a diagnostic and not scored. Floors (unscored, they gate `passed` only): no-redo (src/slug.js sha unchanged; constant re-verified), stale-block (T2), blocked-with-reason (now T5), and a new work-done floor (T4 ends `[x]` and CHANGELOG.md contains 0.1.0), so a run cannot pass A1 by marking `[~]` and stopping. Why the baseline should fail: all 37 recorded baselines record pending tasks only as outcomes, writing the work and then flipping `[ ]->[x]`, usually batched; 34 of 37 never claimed a pending task first. Why the treatment should pass: step 1 of the skill's §Running a task ("Mark it `[~]`") and the Unattended paragraph ("Mark `[~]` before starting a task ... so a crash leaves the file honest") apply without ambiguity to a task with real work. The Context already supplies the reason (a box that can be reclaimed mid-run) without naming the step. Pre-registered in Design Notes: one preflight. If it BLOCKs, exactly one further redesign is allowed; a second BLOCK is recorded as a finding about the scenario, with no A/B, no moved threshold and no re-roll. Issue #184 (handoff from executing to dispatching): not touched; this scenario never reaches dispatch.

risks:
- **Treatment floor:** no treatment trial exists on the repaired instrument. The 16/20 pending-task `[~]` rate comes from pre-repair pools on a fixture with no real-work pending task. The expectation is at least that rate, but it is unmeasured.
- **Ceiling:** the baseline rate of 3/37 on fixture-pending tasks was measured on T3 (no work needed) and the old publish T4. A pending task with real work might draw more spontaneous `[~]` from the baseline; unmeasured until preflight.
- **Grader noise:**
  - The Edit summary truncates `new_string` at 300 characters. `[~] T4` sits 171 characters into a block that starts at T3, 391 into one that starts at T2 with its note attached, and 481 into one that starts at T1. Only those last two whole-list Edit shapes would lose the mark; a whole-file Write renders in full.
  - A `grep '\[~\] T4'` read before any marking would count as a mark.
  - An exotic CHANGELOG writer that is not recognised falls back to "mark anywhere counts".
  - All three are documented in Design Notes.
- **Preflight k:** fixed at 3 (the ledger records that `## Trials` is not honored by preflight). The A/B needs an explicit `--k 10`.
- **Old pools:** they are not comparable (the Setup changed) and must not be pooled with v4.
- **Ledger:** evals/skill-eval-coverage.md and product/ were deliberately not edited; the ledger rows still describe v3.
